title: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness
body:
Read the chapter → [Joshua 22](/bible/joshua/22)

**[Joshua 22:1-3](/bible/joshua/22#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/22#v1)</sup> Then Joshua called the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/joshua/22#v2)</sup> And said unto them, Ye have kept all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, and have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you:
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/joshua/22#v3)</sup> Ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day, but have kept the charge of the commandment of the Lord your God.

- Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh and told them they had kept all that Moses commanded them and obeyed his voice; they had not left their brethren these many days, but kept the charge of the commandment of the Most High.
- The charge was the condition Moses set when these two and a half tribes asked to stay on the other side Jordan: whenever it was time to go to war they had to show up and fight with their brethren, not sit over there while Israel took the land.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 32:20-22](/bible/numbers/32#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/numbers/32#v20)</sup> And Moses said unto them, If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord to war,
    >
    > <sup>[21](/bible/numbers/32#v21)</sup> And will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord, until he hath driven out his enemies from before him,
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/numbers/32#v22)</sup> And the land be subdued before the Lord: then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord.

    Moses said if ye will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord until his enemies be driven out, then afterward ye shall return and be guiltless, and this land shall be your possession.
  - **[Numbers 32:23](/bible/numbers/32#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/numbers/32#v23)</sup> But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out.

    But if ye will not do so, ye have sinned against the Lord, and be sure your sin will find you out.

**[Joshua 22:4-6](/bible/joshua/22#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/joshua/22#v4)</sup> And now the Lord your God hath given rest unto your brethren, as he promised them: therefore now return ye, and get you unto your tents, and unto the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave you on the other side Jordan.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/joshua/22#v5)</sup> But take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, which Moses the servant of the Lord charged you, to love the Lord your God, and to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/22#v6)</sup> So Joshua blessed them, and sent them away: and they went unto their tents.

- Now that the Most High had given rest to their brethren as he promised, there was no war going on, so Joshua sent them home: return ye unto your tents and unto the land of your possession which Moses gave you on the other side Jordan.
- The release came with a charge: take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.
- Rest did not end the duty; if their brethren ever needed them again they had to show up, as all the tribes did show up later in this same chapter.

**[Joshua 22:7-9](/bible/joshua/22#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/22#v7)</sup> Now to the one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given possession in Bashan: but unto the other half thereof gave Joshua among their brethren on this side Jordan westward. And when Joshua sent them away also unto their tents, then he blessed them,
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/22#v8)</sup> And he spake unto them, saying, Return with much riches unto your tents, and with very much cattle, with silver, and with gold, and with brass, and with iron, and with very much raiment: divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/joshua/22#v9)</sup> And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned, and departed from the children of Israel out of Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go unto the country of Gilead, to the land of their possession, whereof they were possessed, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

- Joshua blessed them and sent them away rich: return with much riches unto your tents, with very much cattle, with silver, gold, brass, iron, and very much raiment, and divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren.
- The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

**[Joshua 22:10-12](/bible/joshua/22#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/joshua/22#v10)</sup> And when they came unto the borders of Jordan, that are in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by Jordan, a great altar to see to.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/joshua/22#v11)</sup> And the children of Israel heard say, Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh have built an altar over against the land of Canaan, in the borders of Jordan, at the passage of the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/joshua/22#v12)</sup> And when the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation of the children of Israel gathered themselves together at Shiloh, to go up to war against them.

- When the two and a half tribes came to the borders of Jordan they built a great altar by Jordan, an altar great to see to. They hid nothing; they built it on purpose so that it could be seen.
- When the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation gathered themselves together at Shiloh to go up to war against them. They thought the two and a half tribes had built the altar to worship idols and do their own thing, and they were ready to cleanse it before judgment fell on the whole nation like it had before.

**[Joshua 22:13-14](/bible/joshua/22#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/joshua/22#v13)</sup> And the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest,
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/joshua/22#v14)</sup> And with him ten princes, of each chief house a prince throughout all the tribes of Israel; and each one was an head of the house of their fathers among the thousands of Israel.

- Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes, one head of a chief house from every tribe. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him.
- At Baalpeor the men of Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, bowed down to their gods, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Most High was kindled against Israel.
- One man of Israel was so bold he brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation while they wept before the door of the tabernacle. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit.
- Phinehas saw it, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed from the children of Israel; those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 25:1-3](/bible/numbers/25#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/numbers/25#v1)</sup> And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/numbers/25#v2)</sup> And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/numbers/25#v3)</sup> And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.

    Israel began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, ate of the sacrifices of their gods and bowed down to them, and Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled.
  - **[Numbers 25:4-5](/bible/numbers/25#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/numbers/25#v4)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/numbers/25#v5)</sup> And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.

    The Lord told Moses to take all the heads of the people that were joined to Baalpeor and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that his fierce anger be turned away from Israel.
  - **[Numbers 25:6-9](/bible/numbers/25#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/numbers/25#v6)</sup> And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/numbers/25#v7)</sup> And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand;
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/numbers/25#v8)</sup> And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/numbers/25#v9)</sup> And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.

    Phinehas rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin, and thrust the man of Israel and the woman through, and the plague was stayed; those that died were twenty and four thousand.

**[Joshua 22:15-18](/bible/joshua/22#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/joshua/22#v15)</sup> And they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh, unto the land of Gilead, and they spake with them, saying,
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/joshua/22#v16)</sup> Thus saith the whole congregation of the Lord, What trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to turn away this day from following the Lord, in that ye have builded you an altar, that ye might rebel this day against the Lord?
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/joshua/22#v17)</sup> Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we are not cleansed until this day, although there was a plague in the congregation of the Lord,
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/joshua/22#v18)</sup> But that ye must turn away this day from following the Lord? and it will be, seeing ye rebel to day against the Lord, that to morrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel.

- The delegation asked what trespass is this that ye have committed against the God of Israel, to build you an altar that ye might rebel this day against the Lord. They saw the altar and immediately thought the two and a half tribes were going into idolatry.
- Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us? All those thousands died in that plague, and Israel had just gotten into the land and gotten peace; why would anyone bring that thing back on the nation again?
- Their reasoning was national: if ye rebel today against the Lord, tomorrow he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel. Judgment does not fall on pieces of the nation; [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28) happened to all of us, and they understood that, so they showed up quick, fast, and in a hurry rather than sit around and let it happen.

**[Joshua 22:19-20](/bible/joshua/22#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/joshua/22#v19)</sup> Notwithstanding, if the land of your possession be unclean, then pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord, wherein the Lord’s tabernacle dwelleth, and take possession among us: but rebel not against the Lord, nor rebel against us, in building you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/joshua/22#v20)</sup> Did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel? and that man perished not alone in his iniquity.

- They even offered their own land: if the land of your possession be unclean, pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the Lord and take possession among us, close by where we can keep an eye on you; only rebel not against the Lord, nor build you an altar beside the altar of the Lord our God.
- They cited the proof from their own history: did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone in his iniquity. One man trespassed and the whole nation felt it.

  Precepts:
  - **[Joshua 7:1](/bible/joshua/7#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/7#v1)</sup> But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.

    Achan of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against all the children of Israel.
  - **[Joshua 7:15](/bible/joshua/7#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/joshua/7#v15)</sup> And it shall be, that he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath: because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord, and because he hath wrought folly in Israel.

    He that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath, because he hath transgressed the covenant of the Lord.

**[Joshua 22:21-23](/bible/joshua/22#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/joshua/22#v21)</sup> Then the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh answered, and said unto the heads of the thousands of Israel,
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/joshua/22#v22)</sup> The Lord God of gods, the Lord God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion, or if in transgression against the Lord, (save us not this day,)
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/joshua/22#v23)</sup> That we have built us an altar to turn from following the Lord, or if to offer thereon burnt offering or meat offering, or if to offer peace offerings thereon, let the Lord himself require it;

- The two and a half tribes answered: the LORD God of gods, the LORD God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion or in transgression against the Lord, save us not this day. They put their own lives on the line: if we built this thing in rebellion, put us to death today.
- If we built an altar to turn from following the Lord, or to offer burnt offerings, meat offerings, or peace offerings on it, let the Lord himself require it.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 18:19](/bible/deuteronomy/18#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/18#v19)</sup> And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.

    Whosoever will not hearken unto the words of the Lord, he will require it of him; the Lord requires it whenever you go off.

**[Joshua 22:24-25](/bible/joshua/22#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/joshua/22#v24)</sup> And if we have not rather done it for fear of this thing, saying, In time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the Lord God of Israel?
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/joshua/22#v25)</sup> For the Lord hath made Jordan a border between us and you, ye children of Reuben and children of Gad; ye have no part in the Lord: so shall your children make our children cease from fearing the Lord.

- This is why they built it: for fear of this thing, that in time to come your children might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the LORD God of Israel? The Lord hath made Jordan a border between us and you; ye have no part in the LORD.
- They feared that generations later the children on one side of Jordan would tell the children on the other side that they were not the children of Israel, shutting them out from fearing the Lord, from the temple, the feast days, and the sacrifices.

**[Joshua 22:26-29](/bible/joshua/22#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/joshua/22#v26)</sup> Therefore we said, Let us now prepare to build us an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice:
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/joshua/22#v27)</sup> But that it may be a witness between us, and you, and our generations after us, that we might do the service of the Lord before him with our burnt offerings, and with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings; that your children may not say to our children in time to come, Ye have no part in the Lord.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/joshua/22#v28)</sup> Therefore said we, that it shall be, when they should so say to us or to our generations in time to come, that we may say again, Behold the pattern of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifices; but it is a witness between us and you.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/joshua/22#v29)</sup> God forbid that we should rebel against the Lord, and turn this day from following the Lord, to build an altar for burnt offerings, for meat offerings, or for sacrifices, beside the altar of the Lord our God that is before his tabernacle.

- The altar was not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice; it was a witness between us and you and our generations after us, a memorial, so the two and a half tribes could do the service of the Lord before him in the place he chose, along with the rest of the tribes, and nobody could stop them.
- If anyone ever said to their generations, Ye have no part in the Lord, the answer would stand built in stone: behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifices, but it is a witness between us and you.
- The same thing is happening today with the northern kingdom. Our people left their own witnesses over here: the writings on the Los Lunas stone identify with the northern kingdom, and the traditions, artifacts, practices, laws, and books that are being brought out in the classes all prove our people were here long ago and that they are the children of Israel. Yet with all that proof out there, people still deny it, the very thing the two and a half tribes feared.
- Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Esdras 3:36](/bible/2-esdras/3#v36)**
    > <sup>[36](/bible/2-esdras/3#v36)</sup> Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.

    Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen; only Israel could leave the pattern of the law behind as a witness.
- God forbid that we should rebel against the Lord to build an altar for burnt offerings, meat offerings, or sacrifices, beside the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle: the sacrifices belonged in front of the altar the Most High set in his chosen place.

**[Joshua 22:30-31](/bible/joshua/22#v30)**

> <sup>[30](/bible/joshua/22#v30)</sup> And when Phinehas the priest, and the princes of the congregation and heads of the thousands of Israel which were with him, heard the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake, it pleased them.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/joshua/22#v31)</sup> And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh, This day we perceive that the Lord is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord: now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the Lord.

- When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord.
- Now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD: because they were not going off, nobody had to die that day, and coming from Phinehas that meant everything, because if it had been rebellion he would have been the one to start it.

**[Joshua 22:32-34](/bible/joshua/22#v32)**

> <sup>[32](/bible/joshua/22#v32)</sup> And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the princes, returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead, unto the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and brought them word again.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/joshua/22#v33)</sup> And the thing pleased the children of Israel; and the children of Israel blessed God, and did not intend to go up against them in battle, to destroy the land wherein the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/joshua/22#v34)</sup> And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the Lord is God.

- Phinehas and the princes returned from Gilead to the land of Canaan and brought the children of Israel word again: all is good, the altar is a memorial so the generations after do not forget that our people are on that side Jordan too, and they can come in and keep the feasts and do their sacrifices with us.
- The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt.
- The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God.
